model.notes: Rank-value encoding, max_len=2048, 12 layers, hidden 768. Cell embedding = mean over gene tokens, excluding special tokens.

ceiling.method: empirical: best of {scaled, unscaled} x {raw, pca50, pca128} x {C=1, C=0.1} logistic regression; configuration chosen on a validation carve of the training set (validation), then refit on the full training set and scored once on test
ceiling.note: Won by unscaled/raw/C=0.1. Interpret model scores relative to this: at or above it, the representation adds nothing over standard supervised practice on the raw features.

extra.why_not_group_stratified: predicting donor identity requires donors on both sides of the split, so a donor-disjoint split is impossible by construction. Cells are split within each donor instead.
extra.donor_retention_note: model donor decodability divided by raw-expression donor decodability under the identical readout budget. >1 means the representation surfaces more donor identity than raw expression does at the same capacity.

caveats: Lower is better on this task: the score is how well donor identity can be read out of the representation.
Surfaces 128% of the donor identity that raw expression yields at the same readout capacity -- it makes donor *more* decodable than the untransformed data does, not less.
Internals leak more donor identity than the sanctioned surface does, so the sanctioned surface is hiding nuisance structure rather than removing it.
